abstract:
_Purpose_ – The main objective of this project was to evaluate typhoon-related Tweets’ urgency using sentiment analysis with supervised learning over an artificial neural network.

_Method_ – The researchers implemented artificial neural network and natural language processing techniques for sentiment analysis and evaluation of the urgency score of typhoon-related Tweets. The model’s accuracy on training and validation was evaluated simultaneously. A separate validation using 100 data was done using confusion matrix analysis.

_Results_ – The accuracy of the model in training was at 99.87% and the loss was 0.0074. Validation was conducted simultaneously with the training. It was found that the accuracy of the model was at 99.17% and the loss was 0.0680. The confusion matrix analysis showed that the sensitivity was 97.67% and the specificity was 100%. The positive predictive value was 100% and the negative predicted value was 98.28%. Both false positive and false discovery rates are at 0% while the false-negative rate was at 2.33%. Finally, the F1 score was 98.82% and accuracy was 99%.

_Conclusion_ – The implementation of the architecture of the model was successful; the researchers concluded that the training produced successful results by looking at the high accuracy prediction of the model and the low loss during the simultaneous training and validation, and confusion matrix analysis for the separate validation.

_Recommendations_ – The researchers recommend expanding the vocabulary of the model by adding more diverse data to the dataset when training. The model produced by this study can be used in incident reporting systems that will be helpful during times of typhoon-related disasters.

_Research Implications_ – Using the model produced by the study in incident reporting applications of the government and NGOs will be more efficient than manually looking at typhoon-related posts on Twitter.

bibliographic.title: Evaluating Urgency of Typhoon-Related Tweets Through Sentiment Analysis Using Artificial Neural Networks
bibliographic.venue: International Journal of Computing Sciences Research

content.problem: Responders in the Philippines cannot efficiently find urgent disaster calls on social media because government communication protocols do not standardize social media platforms.
content.proposed_solution: The authors train a feed-forward neural network using supervised sentiment analysis to assign urgency scores between 0 and 1 to typhoon-related tweets.
dataset_testbed: Dataset of 4,020 English and Tagalog tweets from Typhoon Ulysses collected using Tweepy and the Twitter API, split into 3,900 training and 120 validation tweets
Validation dataset of 100 tweets with 43 urgent and 57 non-urgent tweets for confusion matrix analysis

content.claim: The artificial neural network accurately predicts the urgency of typhoon tweets, achieving 99.17 percent validation accuracy and 99 percent accuracy on separate confusion matrix testing.
author_stated_limitations: The model vocabulary is limited by the training dataset diversity and requires expansion to handle diverse multilingual inputs.

evidence.problem_quote: Even though social media platforms are powerful assets in emergency management, there is still a gap on what people in the Philippines are using in actuality and the standard modes of communication and protocols in the government.
evidence.proposed_solution_quote: The main objective of this project is to evaluate typhoon-related Tweets’ urgency using sentiment analysis with supervised learning over an artificial neural network.
evidence.claim_quote: The model’s prediction accuracy during training reached 99.87% with a loss of 0.0074. The validation accuracy reached 99.17% and a loss of 0.0680 (Table 3, Table 4, and Table 5).
author_stated_limitation_quotes: Even though the researchers were able to reach a high accuracy using the model and the preprocessed dataset but it is still recommended for future researchers to expand the vocabulary of the embedding layer by adding more diverse data to the dataset, even more so if the model will process multilingual inputs.
